title: Network Troubleshooting Essentials: DHCP, ICMP, Ping, Traceroute and MTU
summary: Quick revision notes on how DHCP hands out addresses (DORA, leases, relays) and how ICMP powers ping, traceroute, TTL and path MTU discovery. Ends with a cheat sheet of commands and message types.

chapters.title: DHCP and the DORA Exchange
points: DHCP automatically assigns IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server to a host; runs over UDP, server port 67, client port 68
DORA = Discover (client broadcast, src 0.0.0.0 → 255.255.255.255), Offer (server proposes an IP), Request (client broadcast accepting one offer), Acknowledge (server confirms and lease starts)
Request is broadcast on purpose so every other DHCP server that sent an offer learns it was declined and frees that address
Example trace: client 0.0.0.0 sends Discover; server 192.168.1.1 offers 192.168.1.50/24, gw 192.168.1.1, lease 24h; client Requests it; server ACKs
Gotcha: two DHCP servers on one LAN (e.g. a rogue home router) hand out conflicting gateways/DNS, causing random connectivity failures

chapters.title: Leases, Renewal and Relays
points: A lease is the time a client may use an address; at T1 = 50% of lease the client unicasts a Request to renew with the same server
At T2 = 87.5% the client broadcasts a Request to any server (rebind); if the lease expires with no answer it drops the address and restarts DORA
DHCPRELEASE hands the address back early; DHCPDECLINE is sent when the client's ARP check finds the offered address already in use
Relay agent (ip helper-address) forwards broadcast DHCP across routers as unicast to the server, stamping giaddr so the server picks the right scope

Comparison: same-subnet server needs no relay; remote subnets need a relay and a scope per subnet; reservations bind a MAC to a fixed IP while static IPs are configured on the host and must sit outside the pool

chapters.title: ICMP Message Types and Ping
points: ICMP is a layer 3 control protocol (IP protocol number 1) that reports errors and diagnostics; it carries no ports and no user data
Key types: 0 Echo Reply, 3 Destination Unreachable (codes: 0 net, 1 host, 3 port, 4 fragmentation needed and DF set), 8 Echo Request, 11 Time Exceeded, 5 Redirect
Ping sends Echo Request (type 8) and expects Echo Reply (type 0); output shows TTL, round-trip time and packet loss percentage
ping -c 4 host (Linux/macOS) vs ping -n 4 host (Windows); ping -s sets payload size on Linux, -l on Windows
Gotcha: no reply does not mean the host is down, because firewalls often drop ICMP echo; ping failing but TCP working is common

chapters.title: Traceroute and TTL
points: TTL is an IP header field that each router decrements by 1; at 0 the router drops the packet and sends ICMP Time Exceeded (type 11) to the source, which stops routing loops
Traceroute sends probes with TTL 1, 2, 3...; each router that returns Time Exceeded reveals one hop, and the final host replies to end the trace
Linux traceroute sends UDP to high ports by default and the destination answers Port Unreachable (type 3 code 3); Windows tracert sends ICMP Echo; traceroute -I forces ICMP
Commands: traceroute host, tracert host, mtr host (live combined ping and traceroute with loss per hop)
Gotcha: a * * * hop means that router did not reply (rate-limited or filtered), not that the path is broken; if later hops answer, traffic is passing

chapters.title: MTU, Fragmentation and Path MTU Discovery
points: MTU is the largest IP packet a link carries; Ethernet is 1500 bytes, giving TCP MSS 1460 (1500 minus 20 IP and 20 TCP headers)
If a packet exceeds the MTU and DF is not set, the router fragments it; if DF is set, it drops it and returns ICMP type 3 code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) carrying the next-hop MTU
Path MTU Discovery: sender sets DF and shrinks packet size each time it gets type 3 code 4; IPv6 never fragments in routers, using ICMPv6 Packet Too Big
Test the path: ping -M do -s 1472 host (Linux) or ping -f -l 1472 host (Windows); 1472 + 28 header bytes = 1500
Gotcha: firewalls blocking all ICMP create a PMTU black hole where small requests work but large transfers hang; VPN or tunnel overhead lowers MTU, fix with MSS clamping or a lower interface MTU

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: DHCP, ICMP and Path Tools
points: DORA: Discover, Offer, Request, Ack; UDP 67 server, 68 client; renew at 50%, rebind at 87.5%
ICMP types: 0 echo reply, 3 unreachable, 5 redirect, 8 echo request, 11 time exceeded; 3/4 means fragmentation needed
Commands: ping -c 4 / ping -n 4, traceroute / tracert, mtr, ping -M do -s 1472 for MTU test
TTL decrements per router, hits 0 → Time Exceeded; traceroute raises TTL one at a time
Troubleshooting order: 169.254.x.x address means DHCP failed; ping gateway, then remote IP, then name; large transfers hang means check MTU and ICMP filtering
